baseline_finding: Fifteen primary full texts now cover policy explanation, joint facts/rules abduction, formal feature attribution and AXp/CXp duality, policy diagnosis, semantic policy-version differencing and replay, temporal policy evolution, and provenance-based IDS/attribution/reconstruction. Margrave already identifies request contexts whose decisions change across policy versions; the core definition maps directly to a constrained AXp with positive unit literals. The specific local event/rule intervention domain remains a candidate distinction, while its scientific significance is unestablished.
required_action: Complete the collision analysis across remaining formal XAI and policy explanation work; compare TracePolicy's local event/rule core directly with Margrave's semantic differencing; prove a useful policy/temporal-specific property beyond generic AXp sufficiency and minimality, or justify a significant validated domain instantiation.

baseline_finding: Elsevier's current Computers & Security journal page states a moratorium on submissions featuring AI/ML as significant components; the manuscript frames its subject as explainable intrusion detection and must be assessed against this policy.
required_action: Determine with editorial guidance whether explicit non-ML policy reasoning/XAI falls within the moratorium; do not infer acceptance from the 2026 rejection's scope comment.

baseline_finding: The four-way ablation enumerates all cross-products of separate minimal-core families and evaluates unions against the joint intervention table. All 168 unions from 120 selected Docker alerts and all 11 unions from nine controlled fixtures were sufficient; every case had a union equal to a joint minimal core. An independently table-checked witness has two matched sufficient unions and two insufficient crossed unions. For the induced Boolean classifier, the exact criterion is that a union contains a joint minimal sufficient set, a consequence of the upward-closed sufficiency family. This is an exact criterion but not a policy-structure characterization; no independent realistic evaluation exists.
required_action: Derive and verify a nontrivial policy-structure-specific composability result beyond minterm containment; add prespecified realistic scenarios and an untouched evaluation; integrate the finite-sample result and semantic witness with proportionate conclusions.

baseline_finding: The core maps to a constrained AXp on Boolean retention features; finite existence, sufficiency, and deletion minimality follow the generic abductive pattern. This is not a policy-specific theorem. Theorem-by-theorem proof audit, independent oracle checks, edge-case counterexamples, and useful structural composability results remain incomplete.
required_action: Complete theorem-by-theorem proof review, independent small-domain semantic checks, state/update counterexample search, and determine whether policy/temporal semantics support a nontrivial result beyond generic AXp properties.

required_action: Characterize scaling within current scope; implement and differentially verify another exact backend only if scientifically justified.

baseline_finding: Brucker and Petritsch (2011) provide versioned-policy replay/decision comparison; Margrave (Fisler et al., 2005) computes request contexts with changed decisions between policy versions. TracePolicy binds each core to one policy version and currently explains that version's concrete trace decision. A novel differential event/rule explanation and its value remain unestablished.
required_action: Compare TracePolicy's explanation object and guarantees directly against Margrave; decide whether to implement and validate a differential explanation over both policy versions, or keep the contribution strictly decision-local; evaluate realistic policy changes against fair baselines.
